A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReGap/ReMiss research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching results moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v4 reports original backdoor-detection, jailbreaking, transfer, robustness and ablation results in Sections 3.2 and 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, backdoor analysis, ablations and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: The ReGap objective, regularization, suffix search and generator training remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2. New Appendix C explains the relationship to AdvPrompter without modifying the procedure.

E1.justification: AdvBench, HarmBench, the backdoor-detection data and the existing transfer and defense scenarios are retained. Relocating the Llama 3.1 results introduces no additional coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged. GCG and AutoDAN were already absent from v4's Llama 3.1 comparison; v5 explains their absence while retaining the same ReMiss-versus-AdvPrompter results.

E3.justification: The splits, metrics, target models, training budgets and decoding settings match. Section 5.1 adds documentation distinguishing training from testing and specifying no gradient access during testing; it does not establish a revised experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The reference-model ablation, readability and suffix-length analyses, defense tests, ROC analysis and case studies remain. Removing v4's abbreviated main-text Table 2 loses no case-study evidence because the complete examples remain in Table 8.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report a single training run in the hyperparameter appendix, C.6 in v4 and D.6 in v5. No seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted findings and appendix examples are unchanged. For example, Llama 3.1 test ASR@10 remains 40.4% for ReMiss and 27.9% for AdvPrompter, moving from v4 Table 1 to v5 Table 6.

T1.justification: The reward-misspecification definition, Equations 1–5 and Appendix B's objective decomposition are retained. Expanded explanations of implicit rewards and unlikelihood introduce no new mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about reward misspecification, ReGap, ReMiss, attack success, readability and transferability. Replacing 'novel' with 'new' does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 explicitly qualifies the target-loss criticism by referring to success measured through keyword matching. New Appendix C attributes the advantage over AdvPrompter to ReGap within a shared optimization framework, making the comparative interpretation more explicit.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly spells out training/testing access and use of original implementations. Appendix D.7 explains the implementation constraints behind missing GCG/AutoDAN results for Llama 3.1. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, decoding details and code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Andriushchenko et al. (2024) on adaptive attacks. New Appendix C more explicitly positions ReGap as the contribution within an optimization framework shared with AdvPrompter.

P1.justification: v5 adds a short comparison appendix, renumbers subsequent appendices, and makes localized wording and author/publication-header edits. The main narrative structure remains. Appendix C introduces an incorrect 'Figure 9–14' reference to tables.

P2.justification: The Llama 3.1 rows move from Table 1 into a separate appendix Table 6, and the redundant abbreviated example table is removed. Other tables and figures shift with the layout; all ten figures retain their contents.

improvement.justification: v5 makes the contribution relative to AdvPrompter and the limits of the Llama 3.1 comparison easier to assess through Appendices C and D.7, while preserving the evidence. These are modest transparency gains. The new mistaken figure reference slightly harms navigation, but does not outweigh the useful clarifications.
